title: Leaf by Leaf the Tender Spring...
text:
Leaf by leaf the tender spring

restores the greenness of the fields,

and, freed from the ice, the brook flees,

mocking the meadow.


Awakened yesterday to the first song,

the wild sparrow senses its wing,

and through the light that spills and flows

climbs and descends the birdlike scale.


Now the poppy sheds its glow,

and the dandelion its golden plume;

everything throws itself into the feast of color;


only in the clear blue, blurred by nothing,

a torn and slack cloud floats,

like a briefest enclosure of foam.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the spring sonnet's restored green, bird-scale, color feast, and solitary cloud.

title: The Still Solitude, the Dark Bed
text:
The still solitude, the dark bed

crowned with immortal shadows,

the silence spilled through the night,

and the ring of peace, burning and pure.


Ruth holds her uncertain breath,

uncovers her face troubled by pain,

and, shaken by long longings,

presses her hard breast with a hard hand.


Meanwhile Boaz sleeps; his sense,

submerged in mysterious dream,

ignores Ruth's tenacious presence.


But his wakeful heart meditates...

and the fugitive night rushes

toward the clear beds of dawn.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the nocturnal biblical scene of Ruth, Boaz, silence, and approaching dawn.

title: Because I Lost, in Sterile Chances
text:
Because I lost, in sterile chances,

that warm and ripened image

which nature gave me of itself,

entangled in Your voice and Your embraces.


Not even the murmur of Your steps;

nothing now endures inside the heart;

You have become a "Perhaps" in my blackness

and emptied Yourself of being between my arms.


A universe without cardinal points,

the black wind of Genesis supplants

that blond waving of the wheatfields.


And a vertigo of shadow rises

there where Your angelic torrents

perhaps set down their serene foot.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the capitalized devotional You and the loss of a once ripened divine image.

title: Job
text:
He was the one who came in silent solitude,

and, moving his hosts in ambush,

set a snare at my feet, fire to my roof,

and siege around my walled city.


Like rain unleashed on the mountain,

his arrows came down to my breast;

he killed the loves in my bed

and covered my dwelling with darkness.


He changed soft laughter into mournful grief,

converted delights into spoils,

deafened my voice, bound my flight,


wounded the earth and girded it with brambles,

and left nothing burning beneath the sky

but the dark flame of his eyes.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Job-like devastation as siege, arrows, brambles, and a final dark flame.

title: Although Your Name Is Tender as a Kiss
text:
Although your name is tender as a kiss

and gives off fragrance like spilled oil,

and your memory is sweet and desired,

a rich feast for the senses and enchantment;


and it is glory and light, Love, to carry it imprinted

like a seal drawn upon the soul,

all that is not enough for the enamored heart

to reach life.


Only now, Love, lost in your embraces,

beside your breast will it halt its striving:

it will not loosen the nets and bonds,


nor see peace nor enjoy sleep,

until it has peace between your arms

and sleeps in the lap of its Master.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the devotional-erotic seal, bonds, and final rest in the Master's lap.
